paragraphs: Britax Romer Child Safety Seat is a padded child car seat with deep side wings, a molded shell and a harness over the occupant. Its 27,854 polygons and 29,992 vertices go mostly into the curved headrest, stitched seams and buckle, leaving room for a full car interior.

Fabric weave, plastic grain and webbing straps come from 13 texture maps at 4096 x 4096 and 2048 x 2048. The UVs never overlap, so the cover can be recolored or worn without unwrapping again, and CheckMate Pro covers topology and scene setup.

Five versions sit together: the standalone seat, a blue variant, a generic unbranded seat and two scenes with the seat strapped onto car seats. The mounted ones save time when the shot is about installation rather than the product alone. Since 2018 the model has sold 41 times, mostly to people building family car interiors, safety guides and automotive training material.

Bunch of Grapes is a hanging cluster of round berries on a thin woody stem, tapering from its shoulders down to the tip. The 26,653 polygons and 26,116 vertices are spread across dozens of separate berries, each dimpled where it meets its stalk for close food shots.

Twenty-one maps at 4096 x 4096 and 2048 x 2048 carry the waxy bloom on the skins and their slight translucency. StemCell certification means the same materials come through in several renderers, and the clean unwrap lets you push a berry toward overripe without fighting seams.

The page offers 4 color versions: the dark default, plus black, pink and green bunches built on the same shape. Mixing two of them on one plate gives a fruit bowl more variety than a single copy duplicated over and over. Released in 2020, the cluster has found 41 buyers, mostly for wine labels, still lifes, menu visuals and kitchen scenes.

Cellular Tower Site is a complete telecom compound with a lattice mast, antenna panels, equipment cabinets and a fenced gravel pad at its base. Most of its 1,057,154 polygons and 1,063,874 vertices sit in the steel lattice and cable runs, keeping thin members round in tight crops.

Painted steel, galvanized fence wire and concrete come from 10 texture maps at 4096 x 4096, applied over non-overlapping UVs. CheckMate Pro confirms the mesh and naming were inspected, which matters in a scene this dense, where parts of the yard get hidden or swapped.

This is a single build with no alternate versions, meant to be dropped into a landscape as a finished site rather than assembled from pieces. It works best as a mid-ground element in rural road shots or as the hero of a network rollout explainer. Since 2017 it has been bought 41 times by telecom engineers, planners and studios illustrating coverage maps, wireless projects and infrastructure reports.

Dodge Ram Rebel 2016 Pikup is a full-size off-road pickup with the blacked-out grille, raised stance and chunky all-terrain tires of the Rebel trim. The 366,379 polygons and 421,826 vertices go into the grille lettering, arches and suspension, while a simple interior reads through the glass.

Paint, rubber and trim come from 4 maps at 4096 x 4096 and 4096 x 4906, laid out on non-overlapping UVs. CheckMate Pro inspection covers the mesh and setup, so doors, wheels and the cargo bed stay separate named parts to hide or recolor.

The family holds 9 versions: two static Rebel builds, a rigged Rebel, and rigged Ram 1500 trucks with Maya and Cinema 4D rigs. The rest are a simple interior Ram 1500, a rigged 2020 model year pickup, a general rigged Ram 1500 and a plain truck. Pick a rigged file when the truck has to drive through a shot, and a static one for parked scenes. The pickup has been on sale since 2015 and has sold 41 copies, mostly for driving games, ranch scenes and film backgrounds.

Echeveria Agavoides is a compact succulent rosette with thick pointed leaves whose tips blush red, the variety growers call lipstick echeveria. Its 16,670 polygons and 17,528 vertices, all quads, give each fleshy leaf a soft keel and a sharp tip that hold up in macro shots.

Color comes from 5 maps at 4096 x 4096, including the red margins and the faint powdery coating that real echeverias carry. StemCell keeps those materials consistent across renderers, and the clean unwrap allows a quick shift toward a greener or more sun-stressed plant.

Two versions sit on this page: the rosette itself and a Succulent Echeveria Agavoides variant with its own presentation. Both are small enough to scatter across a rock garden or a row of terracotta pots without slowing the viewport. The plant has been available since 2017 and counts 41 purchases, mostly from interior visualizers, florist catalogs and garden design studios.

Hybrid Orchid is a single cymbidium flower spike in soft yellow, with waxy petals, a curled lip and buds tapering toward the tip. At only 2,682 polygons and 2,655 vertices it is light enough to multiply across a florist counter or wedding table freely.

The mesh uses quads and triangles over non-overlapping UVs, and StemCell certification means the petal materials translate cleanly between renderers. With geometry this lean, the lip and the slight cup of each petal carry the realism, and they read best at medium distance.

This family holds 10 versions: yellow, white, green and pink orchids, and four cymbidium variants with fur on the petals. A vanilla orchid and a natural vanilla blossom prepared for extraction scenes round it out. The fur builds suit close-ups, while the plain ones fill background arrangements. Released in 2021, the set has gone to 41 buyers, often for spa interiors, cosmetics packaging and botanical illustration.

IAI Eitan UAV is a large long-endurance drone with a slim fuselage, long straight wings, twin tail booms and a rear pusher propeller. Its 118,559 polygons and 119,387 vertices concentrate on the nose sensor turret, the landing gear and the boom joints, leaving the wings light.

Surface detail comes from 12 maps at 8192 x 8192 and 4096 x 4096, enough to hold panel lines and stenciling on a close flyby. Non-overlapping UVs and a CheckMate Pro rating mean the gray finish can be weathered or retouched without rebuilding the unwrap.

Six versions are on offer: this static aircraft, a rigged Eitan, a rigged drone variant, rigs for Cinema 4D and Maya, and an unrigged drone. The rigged files suit takeoff and flight sequences, the static ones fit hangar and runway stills. On sale since 2016, it has been chosen 41 times for defense documentaries, simulation trainers and military aviation games.

Index Pointing Up Emoji turns the familiar yellow hand sign into a rounded solid, the index finger raised and the others curled. It takes just 559 polygons and 548 vertices, so it drops into a mobile game, sticker pack or motion graphics loop almost free.

Its 5 maps at 1024 x 1024 match the icon's flat cartoon shading, and the clean unwrap lets the yellow become another skin tone. StemCell certification keeps the material identical whether the hand ends up in a game engine or an offline render.

There are 2 versions: the default hand and the Index Finger Pointing Up Emoji, a sibling build of the same gesture. Both work as a pointer in explainer videos, where the raised finger draws the eye to a caption or a button. The emoji came out in 2020 and has been downloaded by 41 buyers for social clips, chat interfaces and presentation slides.

Male Crash Test Dummy 3D Model recreates the jointed mannequin of vehicle safety labs, with bolted joints and calibration targets on head and chest. The 22,154 polygons and 22,719 vertices are split into separate limbs and torso parts, ready for a driver seat or a test sled.

Painted skin, worn joint covers and target decals come from 3 maps at 4096 x 4096. The UVs do not overlap and the model passed CheckMate Pro, so swapping the yellow finish for another test color takes a single texture edit.

The page lists 8 versions: this static dummy, rigged male and humanoid dummies, Maya and Cinema 4D rigs for both, and an unrigged humanoid. Rigged builds can be keyframed through a collision, while the static ones suit seated stills. Since 2015 the dummy has sold 41 times, mostly for automotive safety explainers, insurance graphics and engineering training.

Mens Suit Jacket 3 is a single-breasted business jacket with notched lapels, a buttoned front and flap pockets, shaped around an invisible body. Its 11,958 polygons and 12,374 vertices outline the shoulder line, lapel roll and cuffs, keeping a tailored silhouette in a store window.

Six maps at 4096 x 4096 carry the wool texture and fine stitching, and clean UVs make a new fabric color or check pattern easy. Passing CheckMate Pro means the garment is a clean, closed mesh rather than a loose cloth simulation.

There are 2 versions: this jacket and Mens Suit Jacket 2, a related cut that gives a menswear rack some variety. Neither carries a body, so they slot onto a mannequin, a hanger or your own character. The jacket has been available since 2015 and has gone to 41 buyers, typically tailors, fashion retailers and game teams dressing office or wedding scenes.

Mineral Quartz Collection gathers several quartz specimens in one file, from single terminated points to tight clusters growing out of a rough matrix. The crystals keep the six-sided prisms and pyramid tips that make quartz recognizable, reading correctly on a geology shelf or shop display.

The set is built to the CheckMate specification, which means the meshes, naming and scene layout were prepared to the inspection rules of the marketplace. Clear and milky stones depend on refraction more than texture, so they come alive once a glass shader and strong backlight hit the facets.

Two versions appear here: the original collection and Mineral Quartz Collection 2, which adds a different selection of specimens. Using both gives a museum case or a mineral fair table enough variety that no two crystals look duplicated. On sale since 2019, the collections have been purchased 41 times, mostly by educators, jewelry designers and artists building fantasy caves or meditation scenes.

MPV 4x4 Bushmaster Camo is an Australian protected infantry vehicle with a V-shaped hull, high clearance and a boxy troop compartment. It suits convoy scenes, peacekeeping visuals and military simulation, where a protected vehicle has to look battle ready. The 310,001 polygons and 328,677 vertices cover the heavy wheels, roof hatches, rear door and protective grilles, so it survives a close walkaround.

Its camouflage is painted through 34 maps at 1024 x 1024 and 4096 x 4096, leaving room for mud, dust or unit markings. CheckMate Pro certification confirms clean topology, and the wheels and doors are separate parts ready for posing.

The page groups 4 versions: this camo build, a rigged infantry vehicle, a static twin of it, and a rigged MR6 variant in camouflage. Rigged copies handle convoy and patrol animation, while static ones fill a base or checkpoint scene. Available since 2018, the vehicle has been bought 41 times for military simulators, war games and defense documentaries.

Oculus Quest 2 Standalone VR Headset with Controllers is a matched set of a white visor headset, its strap and two ring-shaped hand controllers. The 23,583 polygons and 24,092 vertices shape the curved visor, the face foam and the tracking rings, so the kit holds up on camera.

The mesh mixes quads and triangles over a clean unwrap, and CheckMate Pro inspection confirms it is tidy and well organized. The headset and both controllers are separate objects, so each can sit in a hand, on a charging stand or on a shelf.

There are 2 versions: this standalone headset and an All in One Gaming Headset edition of the same hardware. Together they suit tech reviews, VR arcade interiors and product comparisons where the shape of the visor needs to be accurate. Released in 2021, the set has been picked up by 41 buyers, mostly for gaming rooms, classroom scenes and tech blogs.

Passenger Steps 2 is an airport stair truck, a small chassis carrying a railed staircase and a covered platform that docks at an aircraft door. Most of the 587,645 polygons and 595,777 vertices go into tread plates, handrails, hydraulic supports and cab details that hold up in close shots.

Paint, rubber and diamond-plate steel come from 26 maps at 4096 x 4096, mapped on non-overlapping UVs that leave room for an airline color scheme. Inspection to CheckMate Pro guarantees clean geometry and a tidy hierarchy, which helps when separating the stair from the chassis.

Six versions sit together: this unit, a TLD ABS 580 stair vehicle, rigged and static ABS 580 cars, another rigged one and the original. The rigged builds suit animated ground handling sequences, the static ones fill a busy apron. The vehicle has been offered since 2016 and has sold 41 copies to airport planners, flight simulators and travel films.

Pedal Harp Instrument 3D Model is a full concert harp with a carved column, a curved neck, a wide soundboard and a pedal box. Its 82,688 polygons and 87,112 vertices go into the scrolled crown, the tuning pins and the strings, which stay straight and evenly spaced.

Gilded carving, polished wood and string colors are carried by 12 maps at 1024 x 1024 and 4096 x 4096, spread across non-overlapping UVs. The harp passed CheckMate Pro review as a clean, organized mesh, so the strings can be separated for animation or hidden for a stylized look.

This is a single build without alternate versions, scaled for an orchestra stage, a wedding venue or a music room. The tall frame makes it a strong vertical accent beside a piano or in a corner of a classical interior. Since 2018 it has found 41 buyers, mostly concert hall visualizers, music educators and animators working on fantasy or period scenes.

Polyhedral Dice Set is a tabletop role-playing kit with the familiar range of shapes, from the pyramid-like tetrahedron to the many-faced icosahedron. With just 2,856 polygons and 2,868 vertices, all quads, the dice have beveled edges and engraved numerals that catch the table light.

Translucent color and printed numbers come from 30 maps at 2048 x 2048, applied without overlaps in the unwrap. The CheckMate Pro rating means the dice are clean separate objects, ready for a physics simulation where they tumble across a board. Because the meshes are so light, a full bag of dice can be scattered through a scene without slowing playback.

The page holds 5 versions: this blue set, yellow, red and violet sets, and a dedicated build for tabletop RPGs. Mixing colors on one table quickly suggests several players sharing a session, each with a favorite set. The dice have been on sale since 2015 and sold 41 times, mostly to board game designers, streamers and animators working on fantasy adventure scenes.

Shipwreck is the corroded hull of a small cargo vessel, its plating torn open, its deck sagging and its mast still standing above the wreck. With 69,893 polygons and 77,224 vertices, the budget goes into torn plating, exposed ribs and debris rather than smooth hull surfaces.

Rust, flaking paint and salt stains come from 12 maps at 8192 x 8192, holding detail from a wide beach shot to a rivet line. The UVs are mixed, so some areas share texture space, although the mesh itself carries the CheckMate Pro mark for clean build quality.

The 6 versions cover a whole wreck site: this hull, a second rusty wreck, two old masts, and cargo wrecks in blue and brown. Masts and hulls can be scattered separately along a coastline to build a ship graveyard. The wreck has been sold 41 times since 2019, mostly for survival games, coastal environments and post-apocalyptic films.

Stone Crusher Machine is a heavy aggregate crusher with a feed hopper on top, a crushing chamber below and a conveyor carrying gravel away. Its 257,254 polygons and 278,905 vertices go into the steel frame, belt rollers, walkways and guard rails that keep it believable at quarry scale.

Painted steel, rust and dust are carried by 30 maps at 2048 x 2048 on non-overlapping UVs. CheckMate Pro status means clean topology and sensibly named parts, so the conveyor or the hopper can be hidden or animated alone.

It comes as a single build with no alternate versions, ready for a quarry, a mining site or a road construction yard. Piles of gravel and a dump truck nearby are all it needs to tell the story. The machine has been offered since 2018 and has sold 41 times, chiefly to mining equipment dealers, engineering firms and construction game studios.

Tesla Model S Chassis 2 shows the electric sedan stripped to its rolling skateboard: flat battery pack, axle drive units, suspension and wheels. The 114,144 polygons and 125,133 vertices describe the battery enclosure, subframes, control arms and brake discs, the parts an engineering cutaway needs to make clear.

Metal, rubber and painted parts come from 4 maps at 4096 x 4096 and 2048 x 2048, mapped without overlaps. Being CheckMate Pro certified, the chassis arrives with parts separated and named, so the battery lifts out for an exploded view.

This is one build without alternate versions, aimed at technical rather than showroom shots. The low battery floor and the wide track show clearly from a three-quarter angle, which is where most cutaway renders are framed. It pairs well with a translucent body shell for explaining where the weight sits and how power reaches the wheels. Since 2015 it has been purchased 41 times, mostly by engineering students, electric vehicle explainers and technology journalists.

Yellow Poplar Old Tree Summer is a mature tulip poplar in full leaf, with a tall straight trunk, furrowed bark and a rounded crown. Its 1,376,835 polygons and 2,747,135 vertices are almost all foliage, with leaves modeled rather than painted on cards, so the canopy survives a low camera.

Bark, leaf color and translucency come from 9 maps at 2048 x 2048 and 1024 x 1024. The UVs are mixed, with many leaves sharing the same texture space, which is the usual way to keep a tree this large manageable. The CheckMate Pro mark confirms the trunk and branch geometry were checked for clean construction.

Four versions grow from one species: this summer tree, an autumn tree in yellow leaf, a second autumn poplar and a realistic poplar. Placing a summer and an autumn copy in neighboring shots makes a quick seasonal transition. The tree went on sale in 2015 and has been planted in 41 customer projects, mostly parks, campus renders and estate landscapes.

Aluminium Cans Collection lines up drink cans in several common formats, from slim cans to standard and tall ones. Each can has the rolled rim, the ring pull on a recessed lid and the domed base, details a label designer checks before anything else.

The bundle passed CheckMate Pro inspection, so the cans arrive as clean, closed meshes that accept any label artwork. Brushed metal lids and a printable body surface make them a ready starting point for packaging mockups, where designs get swapped often. A wet shader with condensation droplets turns the same cans into a cold drink close-up.

It is a single collection without alternate versions, and the cans can be split apart and used on their own. Arranged in a cooler, on a store shelf or crushed beside a recycling bin, they cover most beverage scenes. On sale since 2017, the collection has been bought 40 times by packaging designers, beverage startups and product renderers.

Anodized Hydraulic Cylinder 3 is a compact actuator with a colored anodized barrel, a polished chrome rod and clevis mounts at both ends. The 14,526 polygons and 14,999 vertices, all quads, keep the barrel round, the threaded end caps crisp and the hose ports clearly defined.

The colored aluminum finish and the mirror rod come from 4 maps at 4096 x 4096 over non-overlapping UVs. Its CheckMate Pro rating reflects the clean quad layout, which also makes the rod easy to slide in and out for a stroke animation.

The family spans 8 versions in different sizes and finishes: this cylinder, numbered siblings 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, and the original. A row of them fits a robotics lab, a press brake or an excavator arm, and mixing lengths makes a mechanism look properly engineered. Since 2016 the part has found 40 buyers among machine designers, robotics teams and industrial animators.

Aqueduct Section Greco Roman is a stretch of ancient stone aqueduct carried on tall round arches, with a water channel running along the top. Its 318,423 polygons and 349,436 vertices model individual blocks, worn edges and each arch's wedge stones, holding up in a low shot of the spans.

Weathered limestone, moss and stains come from 6 maps at 4096 x 4096 on a clean, non-overlapping unwrap. It carries the CheckMate Pro stamp, so the arches can be duplicated end to end into a longer run without trouble in the geometry.

This comes as one section with no alternate versions, designed to repeat across a valley until it reaches the length you need. Paired with cypress trees and a dusty road it sets a Mediterranean scene in minutes. Available since 2016, the section has been bought 40 times, mostly by history documentaries, educational publishers and studios building ancient Rome for games.

B-25 Mitchell US Medium Bomber is the twin-engine Second World War bomber with a glazed nose, twin tail fins and gun positions along the fuselage. The 190,166 polygons and 193,976 vertices define the radial engine cowlings, framed nose glass, turrets and gear, enough for a slow orbit. The bomber suits war documentaries, airshow visuals and flight simulation scenes set over the Pacific or North Africa.

Camouflage paint, bare metal and markings come from 20 maps at 8192 x 8192 and 4096 x 4096, so nose art repaints cleanly. CheckMate Pro certification means the airframe is a clean, carefully grouped build.

The page offers 3 versions: this static bomber, a rigged Mitchell and a second rigged bomber build. The rigged files are made for formation flying and takeoff sequences, while the static one suits airfield or museum stills. On sale since 2017, the aircraft has 40 sales behind it, largely from war documentaries, flight simulators and history channels.

Big Agave Tequilana Blue Agave Plant is a large rosette of stiff blue-gray leaves tipped with dark spines, the plant behind tequila. Its 67,495 polygons and 67,496 vertices go into the long tapering leaves and their serrated teeth, which make the plant look dangerous. Planted in rows it builds a tequila farm field, and a single plant anchors a desert garden render.

The powdery blue surface and dry leaf tips come from 8 maps at 4096 x 4096, applied over non-overlapping UVs. Being StemCell certified, the agave carries consistent PBR materials into several render engines without manual repair.

The page combines 4 versions: this blue agave, two Agave americana century plants in big and large sizes, and a large blue agave. Planted in rows they form a tequila field, while a single specimen anchors a desert garden or a hacienda courtyard. Since 2020 the plant has sold 40 copies, mostly to landscape designers, distillery visualizers and desert scene builders.

Blank Four Way Signpost Black is a tall black post topped with arrow-shaped boards pointing four ways, each left blank for place names. The 14,201 polygons and 14,216 vertices give the arrows beveled edges, the post a cap and each board its bolts, so it looks solid.

Four maps at 4096 x 4096 paint the wood and metal, and the clean UVs leave each arrow face free for text, logos or distances. The signpost holds a CheckMate Pro rating, meaning the mesh is clean and the boards are separate pieces you can rotate.

Two versions share the page: this black post and a red signpost with 4 arrows in the same layout. Blank boards make the sign useful for infographics, wayfinding concepts and decision metaphors in explainer videos. Listed in 2017, it has reached 40 buyers, often teams making motivational slides, travel graphics and park maps.

Boeing 787-8 All Nippon is the Dreamliner in blue and white All Nippon Airways livery, with raked wingtips and serrated engine nacelles. The 404,013 polygons and 414,121 vertices shape the flexing wing, cockpit windows and gear bays, so the airliner holds detail on the ramp.

Livery, panel lines and engine metal are painted across 32 maps at 4096 x 4096 with non-overlapping UVs. A CheckMate Pro rating confirms the airframe is cleanly modeled and organized, so doors, gear and control surfaces are easy to find and move.

With thirty versions this is a large family: United Airlines, Japan Airlines, British Airways, ANA and generic liveries, static and rigged. Maya and Cinema 4D get rigs of their own, and a standalone landing gear assembly is included. Choosing between them comes down to the airline and to whether the aircraft must taxi and fly. The jet went on sale in 2016 and has sold 40 times, chiefly for airport visualization, flight simulators and aviation documentaries.

Business Jet Cessna Model 680 Sovereign is a midsize Citation with a T-tail, two rear-mounted engines and a long row of oval cabin windows. The 147,661 polygons and 153,154 vertices define the slim wing, the airstair door and the tail fairings behind its recognizable apron profile.

Paint stripes, metal and glass are carried by 17 maps at 8192 x 8192 and 4096 x 4096, so a new owner's scheme drops in. Clean modeling earned it CheckMate Pro, and the moving surfaces are separate parts.

The page groups 8 versions: static and rigged Sovereign jets under several names, Citation Sovereign builds, and a corporate transport with an interior. Use the interior variant for cabin shots, the rigged builds for taxi and flight, and the static ones for still frames. Since 2017 the jet has found 40 buyers, mostly for charter company renders, flight training and luxury travel scenes.

Cell Tower is a freestanding steel telecom mast crowned with panel antennas, microwave dishes and a climbing ladder running up one side. Its 951,196 polygons and 956,459 vertices are spent on bolted joints, cable trays and antenna mounts, so it looks engineered against the sky.

Galvanized steel and painted antenna housings come from 7 maps at 4096 x 4096, mapped with no overlaps. Its CheckMate Pro grade guarantees a carefully built mesh, so whole antenna arrays can be deleted or duplicated to match a specific carrier setup.

This tower comes alone, without sister versions, and stands on its own without a fenced yard around it. Paired with an equipment shelter and a fence, it becomes a full rural relay site. That makes it easy to place on a rooftop, a hillside or beside a highway in a wide landscape. Offered since 2017, it has 40 purchases behind it from telecom operators, tower engineers and documentary producers covering mobile networks.

Classic Skateboard Generic is a standard popsicle deck with a kicked nose and tail, metal trucks and urethane wheels. The 21,338 polygons and 21,908 vertices, all quads, round the deck edges, kingpin bushings and wheel bearings for a close look underneath.

Grip tape, deck graphics and scuffed trucks come from 18 maps at 4096 x 4096 and 4000 x 4000. With non-overlapping UVs the bottom graphic takes your own artwork, and CheckMate Pro confirms a clean, separable set of parts. Deck, trucks and wheels come apart, so a kickflip or a broken board can be staged.

The 4 versions cover different rides: this classic deck, a classic shape board, a shorter cruiser and a longboard with custom art. Leaning one against a wall or dropping it at the top of a ramp sets a skate park scene quickly. Available since 2017, the board was bought 40 times, often by sports game developers, streetwear designers and youth culture animators.

Containers Collection groups standard steel shipping containers with corrugated walls, corner castings and locking bars on the double doors. They stack the way real boxes do at a port, so a yard, a ship deck or an industrial backdrop comes from one file.

The bundle carries a CheckMate Pro rating, which means the containers are clean meshes with sensible pivots for stacking and rotating. Corrugation and door hardware are modeled, so a raking sunset light picks out the ribbed walls the way it does on a real terminal. Rust and dents can be added in texturing to age the stacks for a harbor at the end of its working life.

Three versions exist: the first collection and two follow-up sets numbered 2 and 3, each with its own mix of boxes. Combining all of them gives a container terminal enough variety to avoid obvious repeats. On sale since 2015, the series has 40 buyers, mostly logistics firms, port planners and game studios building docks and smuggling levels.

Diving Equipment 3 is a set of scuba gear built around an air tank, its regulator and hoses, and the harness that carries it. Its 32,393 polygons and 33,009 vertices go into the valve, the pressure gauge and the coiled hoses, the details divers look at first.

Rubber, painted metal and fabric straps come from 6 maps at 4096 x 4096 over non-overlapping UVs. CheckMate Pro approval confirms clean modeling, and separate pieces let the gear be arranged on a dock, a boat deck or a diver.

There is one build and no alternates, sized to sit beside a dive center counter or on the back of a boat. Underwater, the kit can be attached to a character for a reef scene, and a few bubbles from the regulator complete the effect. Since 2016 the gear has gone to 40 buyers, mostly dive schools, travel promoters and game developers working on ocean levels.

Electric Light Bulb is a classic pear-shaped incandescent bulb with a clear glass envelope, a coiled filament on its supports and a threaded screw base. The 7,538 polygons and 7,569 vertices keep the glass smooth and the base threads crisp, which matters when a bulb fills the frame.

Glass, brass and the filament glow come from 3 maps at 2048 x 2048, mapped without overlaps. It was certified CheckMate Pro, so the filament is a separate object that can be given an emissive material and switched on in an animation.

The page lists 4 versions: this clear bulb, a standard bulb, a matte frosted bulb and a second electric bulb build. Clear glass suits idea and innovation graphics, while the matte one reads better under a lamp shade. Released in 2018, the bulb has 40 sales, typically from motion designers, lighting retailers and teachers explaining electricity.

Fescue Grass is a patch of fine-bladed turf grass, the kind that covers lawns, roadsides and the edges of sports fields. Its 1,169,388 polygons and 2,143,864 vertices are almost entirely individual blades, bending at different heights so the patch never looks like carpet. Tips come out slightly lighter than the base, which helps when sunlight arrives low.

A single map at 1500 x 1500 colors every blade, and the mixed UVs let thousands share it, keeping memory low for a dense mesh. It passed CheckMate Pro, so the clump can be scattered or instanced across terrain without hidden geometry problems.

There are no alternate versions, just this patch designed to tile across a lawn or meadow with a scatter tool. Up close it fills the foreground of a garden shot, and from further back it softens the edges of paths and buildings. The grass has been available since 2016 and counts 40 buyers among landscape architects, archviz artists and environment modelers.

Hawaiian Leis Collection gathers several flower garlands of the kind given to visitors on arrival in the islands, each strung from closely packed blossoms. The leis hang in soft loops, so they can rest on a neck, drape over a hotel bed or lie on a luau table.

The set carries the CheckMate Pro rating, meaning the garlands are clean, closed meshes rather than scattered petals. Bright tropical colors make them stand out against white shirts and sand, and they still read at small size in a wide beach shot.

It is a single collection with no alternate versions, and each lei can be pulled out and used alone. Placed around a character's neck they instantly signal a Hawaiian holiday, a graduation or a wedding. In the catalog since 2016, the collection has sold 40 copies, mostly to travel agencies, resort visualizers and animators of island stories.

Hockey Goalie Mask Bauer is a modern ice hockey goaltender helmet with a molded shell, a steel cage over the face and padding inside. The shell carries the vents, ridges and chin cup that make a goalie mask recognizable on the ice or on a bench between periods.

The model carries a CheckMate Pro rating, which means the shell, cage and straps are clean separate meshes. The cage bars stay straight and evenly spaced, a detail that matters because viewers look straight through them at the player's eyes. Under arena lights the glossy shell and the matte cage react differently, so the mask holds up in a dramatic close-up.

A second version shares the page: an all-black edition of this mask with the same shape. A dark shell is a good base for custom goalie art, which every netminder treats as a personal signature. On sale since 2016, the mask has found 40 buyers, mostly hockey game studios, sports illustrators and arena visualizers.

House Construction On Blueprints shows a house under construction on spread-out architectural drawings, its frame of studs and rafters unfinished. The 52,389 polygons and 53,938 vertices go into the timber framing, roof trusses and curled sheet edges, so plan and building read together.

Paper texture, printed lines and raw wood come from 11 maps at 4096 x 4096 and 2048 x 2048, laid out on non-overlapping UVs. It is a CheckMate Pro asset, so the frame and the drawings are clean separate pieces that can be animated growing from the page.

There is a single version with nothing to choose between, built as a ready-made metaphor rather than a real site. It fits mortgage, real estate and construction explainers, where an image has to say that planning becomes building. Since 2017 the scene has been purchased 40 times, chiefly by builders, architects and financial content teams.

Human Full Respiratory System traces the airway from the nasal cavity and throat down through the trachea and bronchi into both lungs. Its 37,681 polygons and 37,789 vertices shape the bronchial tree, the lobes of each lung and the windpipe's cartilage rings in clear order.

An unusually large set of 80 maps at 8192 x 8192 and 4096 x 4096 provides tissue color, moist surfaces and fine vessel detail. Its UV islands stay separate, and CheckMate Pro ensures each structure is a clean, named part to isolate or make transparent. The trachea, bronchi and lungs can be shown together or one at a time for a lesson.

It comes as one build without alternate versions, scaled for medical education rather than for a full body. Teachers can fade the lungs to show the bronchi, and animators can scale them to suggest breathing.
